group.title: Body and clothes
group.tagline: What you have and what you wear
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: The top part of your body, with your eyes, ears and mouth.
examples: She wore a warm hat on her {head}.
wrong: I put my shoes on my head and walked to school.

words.meaning: The front of your head, with your eyes, nose and mouth.
examples: Wash your {face} with cold water.
wrong: He smiled with his face on the back of his head.

words.meaning: The part of your body that you see with.
examples: She has one blue {eye} and one green eye.
wrong: I closed my eyes so I could see the picture better.

words.meaning: The part of your body that you hear with.
examples: He held the phone to his {ear}.
wrong: I listen to music with my nose, not my ears.

words.meaning: The part of your face that you smell and breathe with.
examples: The cold air made my {nose} red.
wrong: I smell the flowers with my ears.

words.meaning: The part of your face that you eat and speak with.
examples: Don’t talk with food in your {mouth}.
wrong: She opened her mouth to hear the music.

words.meaning: One of the hard white things in your mouth that you bite with.
examples: I brush every {tooth} twice a day.
wrong: He walks to work on his teeth.

words.meaning: The thin threads that grow on your head.
examples: My sister has long black {hair}.
wrong: He cut his hair with a spoon, so it was very short.

words.meaning: The part at the end of your arm, with fingers.
examples: Raise your {hand} if you know the answer.
wrong: She wears her socks on her hands to walk.

words.meaning: The long part of your body between your shoulder and your hand.
examples: He carried the baby in his {arms}.
wrong: I kick the ball with my arm.

words.meaning: One of the long parts of your body that you walk on.
examples: My {legs} hurt after the long walk.
wrong: Fish have strong legs for swimming.

words.meaning: The part at the end of your leg that you stand on.
examples: This shoe is too small for my {foot}.
wrong: I wear a glove on my foot.

words.meaning: One of the five long parts at the end of your hand.
examples: She wears a ring on her {finger}.
wrong: A hand has ten fingers and two thumbs.

words.meaning: The part of your body behind you, from your neck to your legs.
examples: He carries his bag on his {back}.
wrong: I can see my own back in front of me.

words.meaning: The part of your body between your head and your shoulders.
examples: She wore a scarf around her {neck}.
wrong: He put his watch on his neck to check the time.

words.meaning: The part of your body between your neck and your arm.
examples: The bag hung from her {shoulder}.
wrong: My shoulders are at the end of my feet.

words.meaning: The part in the middle of your leg where it bends.
examples: I fell and hurt my {knee}.
wrong: She bends her knee to move her fingers.

words.meaning: All of a person or an animal, from head to feet.
examples: Exercise is good for your {body}.
wrong: My body is a small room in my house.

words.meaning: The part inside your chest that moves blood around your body.
examples: His {heart} beat fast after the race.
wrong: My heart is in my left shoe.

words.meaning: The outer cover of your body.
examples: Sun cream protects your {skin}.
wrong: He took off his skin and put on a shirt.

words.meaning: A piece of clothing for the top of your body, often with buttons.
examples: He wore a white {shirt} to the meeting.
wrong: I wear my shirt on my feet.

words.meaning: A piece of clothing that is a top and a skirt in one.
examples: She wore a red {dress} to the party.
wrong: He put the dress on the table and ate it.

words.meaning: A piece of clothing that hangs from the waist.
examples: Her {skirt} is long and blue.
wrong: I wear a skirt on my head to keep warm.

words.meaning: A piece of clothing that covers each leg separately.
examples: These {trousers} are too long for me.
wrong: He wore his trousers on his arms.

words.meaning: A covering for your foot, often made of leather.
examples: Take off your {shoes} at the door.
wrong: I put my shoes on my hands to write.

words.meaning: A soft covering for your foot that you wear inside a shoe.
examples: I can only find one {sock}.
wrong: She wears her socks over her shoes.

words.meaning: A thing you wear on your head.
examples: Wear a {hat} in the sun.
wrong: He wore his hat on his foot.

words.meaning: A long warm piece of clothing that you wear outside.
examples: Put on your {coat}; it’s snowing.
wrong: I wear my coat in the hot shower.

words.meaning: A warm piece of clothing for the top of your body, often made of wool.
examples: Grandma made me a {sweater}.
wrong: I wear a thick sweater when it is very hot.

words.meaning: A long piece of cloth that you wear around your neck.
examples: Wrap a {scarf} around your neck.
wrong: She wore her scarf on her feet like shoes.

words.meaning: A covering for your hand, with a part for each finger.
examples: I lost a {glove} in the snow.
wrong: He wears gloves on his ears.

words.meaning: A long thin band you wear around your waist.
examples: These trousers need a {belt}.
wrong: I wear a belt on my head to hold my hat.

words.meaning: A small bag sewn into clothes, to keep things in.
examples: My keys are in my {pocket}.
wrong: I put the car in my pocket.

words.meaning: A small round thing that closes a shirt or coat.
examples: A {button} fell off my coat.
wrong: I eat a button for lunch.

words.meaning: A container made of cloth, paper or plastic, used to carry things.
examples: She put her books in her {bag}.
wrong: I carry my bag inside my pocket.

words.meaning: A thing you hold over your head to stay dry in the rain.
examples: Take an {umbrella}; it’s raining.
wrong: I use an umbrella to cook rice.

words.meaning: Two pieces of glass in a frame that help you see.
examples: I can’t read without my {glasses}.
wrong: She wears glasses to hear better.

words.meaning: To have clothes, shoes or glasses on your body.
examples: I {wear} a uniform at work.
wrong: I wear a sandwich for breakfast.

words.meaning: Higher than most people or things.
examples: My brother is very {tall}.
wrong: The baby is tall, so she is the smallest in the room.

words.meaning: Not tall or not long.
examples: My hair is {short} this summer.
wrong: The film was short, so it lasted five hours.
